spec.description: A dashboard to display data exported by Speedtest Tracker

spec.title: Speedtest Results
spec.description:
Download speed - measures how quickly you can pull data from a server on the internet to your device.

Upload speed - measures how quickly you send data from your device to the internet.

spec.title: Download Speed
spec.description: Download speed - measures how quickly you can pull data from a server on the internet to your device.

spec.title: Upload Speed
spec.description: Upload speed - measures how quickly you send data from your device to the internet.

spec.title: Response Time
spec.description: Also called latency, ping is the reaction time of your connection - that is, how quickly your device gets a response after you've sent out a request.

spec.title: Ping
spec.description: Also called latency, ping is the reaction time of your connection - that is, how quickly your device gets a response after you've sent out a request.

spec.title: Jitter
spec.description:
Also called Packet Delay Variation (PDV), jitter is a measure of the variability in ping over time.
This metric shows the average difference between consecutive latency measurements.

spec.title: Packet Loss
spec.description: Packet loss occurs when a packet of data being sent over the internet is not received or is incomplete. This is described in the percentage of packets lost compared to packets sent.

spec.title: Ping Jitter
spec.description:
Also called Packet Delay Variation (PDV), jitter is a measure of the variability in ping over time.
This metric shows the average difference between consecutive latency measurements.

spec.title: Upload Latency
spec.description:
Low - Minimum Latency (formerly, Latency) measures the best case latency for the user at the time they decide to take a Speedtest.

Avg - Primary-Server Latency is the interquartile mean (IQM or midmean) of the idle latency tests taken prior to the download portion of a Speedtest.

High - Multi-server latency measures latency to multiple connections and then takes an average.
